abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Background</jats:title><jats:p>Hessian fly (<jats:italic>Mayetiola destructor</jats:italic>) is one of the most destructive pests of wheat. The genes encoding 12-oxo-phytodienoic acid reductase (OPR) and lipoxygenase (LOX) play critical roles in insect resistance pathways in higher plants, but little is known about genes controlling resistance to Hessian fly in wheat.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>In this study, 154 F<jats:sub>6:8</jats:sub>recombinant inbred lines (RILs) generated from a cross between two cultivars, ‘Jagger’ and ‘2174’ of hexaploid wheat (2n = 6 × =42; AABBDD), were used to map genes associated with resistance to Hessian fly. Two QTLs were identified. The first one was a major QTL on chromosome 1A (<jats:italic>QHf.osu-1A</jats:italic>), which explained 70% of the total phenotypic variation. The resistant allele at this locus in cultivar 2174 could be orthologous to one or more of the previously mapped resistance genes (<jats:italic>H9</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>H10</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>H11</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>H16</jats:italic>, and<jats:italic>H17</jats:italic>) in tetraploid wheat. The second QTL was a minor QTL on chromosome 2A (<jats:italic>QHf.osu-2A</jats:italic>), which accounted for 18% of the total phenotypic variation. The resistant allele at this locus in 2174 is collinear to an<jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic>-containing-fragment translocated from chromosome 2N of<jats:italic>Triticum ventricosum</jats:italic>(2n = 4 × =28; DDNN) in Jagger. Genetic mapping results showed that two<jats:italic>OPR</jats:italic>genes,<jats:italic>TaOPR1-A</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>TaOPR2-A</jats:italic>, were tightly associated with<jats:italic>QHf.osu-1A</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>QHf.osu-2A,</jats:italic>respectively. Another<jats:italic>OPR</jats:italic>gene and three<jats:italic>LOX</jats:italic>genes were mapped but not associated with Hessian fly resistance in the segregating population.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>This study has located two major QTLs/genes in bread wheat that can be directly used in wheat breeding programs and has also provided insights for the genetic association and disassociation of Hessian fly resistance with<jats:italic>OPR</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>LOX</jats:italic>genes in wheat.</jats:p></jats:sec>
title: Genetic association of OPRgenes with resistance to Hessian fly in hexaploid wheat
